messages:
Samir: quick thread — I'm digging into our p95/p99 divergence between replay and our synthetic driver. replay shows stable p95 at our microbatch=8 profile but synthetic spikes. suspect kernel selection flip + KV cold miss patterns. anyone seen similar?
June: seen this before. synthetic driver creates uniform seq lengths and saturates kernel A, replay has more short-prefix traffic so kernel B gets chosen sometimes.
Alex: +1. also microbatch sizing can push kernel heuristic into different code paths. we have a breakpoint in kernel_selector: if avg_seq < 64 -> use fused-attn-v2 else unfused. that can flip mid-run if mix changes.
Priya: do we have a profiler trace from the failing run? can you paste flamegraph?
Samir: pasted short trace from the synthetic run:
```
time | kernel_selector -> fused-attn-v2
op   | matmul(512x512)  42%
op   | softmax          12%
op   | kv_cache_write    6%
```
replay run trace:
```
time | kernel_selector -> unfused-attn
op   | matmul(512x512)  28%
op   | kv_cache_write   22%  (lots of mem copies)
op   | wait/host-sync   18%
```
June: that kv_cache_write jump screams cold cache and extra host<->device copies. synthetic probably warms cache differently.
Mika: another angle: our batching heuristic currently clamps microbatch size by observed latency SLO at 95th. If synthetic driver underestimates variability, clamp allows bigger microbatches which degrade tail.
Alex: right — synthetic runs often have very narrow P50 distribution which lets the autoscaler microbatch up. real traffic has long tail tails so p99 suffers.
Priya: what about replay fidelity? are we replaying token gaps and inter-arrival jitter? naive replay often omits client-side think times and backpressure.
Samir: replay uses request timestamps but we didn't preserve client-side pacing for some customers. that likely explains differences. plan: add a jittered replay mode that replays original arrival times and has an option to preserve pacing.
perf-bot: CI perf check (1876543950): baseline vs head — p95 +12ms, p99 +47ms, fail if degradation >10ms.
June: oof CI flagged it. Samir can you isolate whether it's kernel selection or KV paths? maybe run with env KERNEL_FORCE=fused-attn to see delta.
Samir: running forced-kernel test now. attaching results in a sec.
Alex: also try forcing KV_CACHE_PINNED=1 to avoid host copies, and microbatch=4 vs 8. want a 2x2 matrix: {kernel: forced, kv: pinned} x {mb=4,mb=8}.
Mika: agree. also capture tail traces with our tail-profiler (low-overhead sampling). we need to see per-request state when p99 fires.
Priya: small note on measurement: when computing p99 across runs, make sure you aggregate at the request level not batch-level averages. some folks average within batches then compute p99 and that underestimates tails.
Samir: good call. I'll run the matrix, collect tail samples, and re-run CI with jittered replay. will update thread with results.
June: thanks. if forcing kernel fixes p99, we should add a safety: if p99 worsens after heuristic-driven kernel flip, stick to previous kernel per-model for 15m cooldown. avoid oscillation.
Alex: and add a regression test that compares replayed-p99 vs jittered-replay-p99 to catch replay-hygiene issues in PRs.
Samir: plan set. will follow up with numbers. :thumbsup:
Priya: :raised_hands:
perf-bot: perf run queued (1876543982)
Samir: queued runs finished — preliminary: forcing fused-attn reduced p99 by ~35ms on synthetic but only ~8ms on replayed-jittered. KV_PINNED gave ~20ms improvement on replay.
June: suggests two root causes: kernel flip + host-copy chatter. next step: short-term mitigations (force kernel cooldown + enable pinned KV on models w/ hot-KV) and long-term: make kernel_selector cost model use tail-weighted estimators.
Alex: perfect. let's draft the patch: cooldown policy + tail-aware selection. I can take kernel_selector, Samir can own KV_PINNED rollout.
Samir: assigning. I'll open a PR with test harness that runs jittered replay vs synthetic and fails if p99 delta > 5%.
Mika: nice. one more thing: add a note to the benchmarking docs about synthetic driver assumptions and how to pick modes (warmup vs cold-start vs paced). few infra folks were bitten by this.
Samir: will add to docs. closing for now, will post PR links here.
